assumptions.claim: 0002's all-version range 8.0 through 2025 and engineer-day table were planning assumptions for a Python reader without an IDE, not an agreed scope endpoint or measured full-goal schedule.

Reading representations, dependency models and public wrappers can be shared with writing. Serialization, creation defaults, preservation and rebuild correctness are additional obligations; an encoder is not assumed to cost the same as a decoder.

Version-dependent cost scales with evidenced incompatible layouts, semantics and build/runtime combinations, not a fixed multiplier per release. Neither 2024 nor all versions has a measured number of such strata.

A strict 2024 editing-format scope is a comparison scenario only. If it must still preserve non-2024 originals, native older encoders/round-trip rules re-enter the work; conversion alone does not discharge the requirement.

No engineering-day range is defensible for incremental writing without at least one independently established semantic edit/encode/integrity contract and measured implementation/validation effort. Unknown costs are null, never zero.

Acquisition/availability, engineering labor and machine/native runtime should be reported in different units. A missing source, builder, license or runtime is a blocking dependency, not a small fixed labor surcharge.

version_axes.original_save_version: Per-original artifact evidence, independently pinned before exposure; unknown stays unknown. vers, LVSR and project LVVersion declarations are distinct evidence, not automatically interchangeable.
version_axes.editing_format: The format/layout actually decoded and emitted by the offline writer; an internal text/IR version is not the native save version. Creation has an explicit requested target save version. 2024 comprises Q1/Q3/patch possibilities, not a proven single encoding.
version_axes.validation_runtime: Actual LabVIEW build/OS, modules, target, dependencies and licenses of a separate trusted validation job; a 2026 reader of older input is not a 2024 writer or proof that an older save format was preserved.
same_save_version_output_checks: Preserve and hash untouched originals outside writable workspaces; freeze full original/dependency manifests and per-file independently established save versions.

Freeze requested semantic changes, native object maps, unrelated-object/file invariants and narrowly permitted metadata changes. Return every produced, missing and unexpected file with hashes and original/output locators.

Independently establish output save format for every modified/propagated source and equality with its original (creation equals requested target). Compare all available raw declarations; unresolved or conflicting fields remain unverified, not a passed equality check.

Use a separate provisioned native job on disposable frozen outputs, preferably the original-version environment, to record load without broken arrow, compilation/build, discriminating I/O and target execution separately. Record any conversion prompt/resave and keep the unsaved output frozen; newer-runtime loading alone cannot establish same-save-version compatibility.

For rebuilt distributions, separately record source versions, build toolchain and output format/API/runtime compatibility; build output byte equality is not generally assumed, and permitted timestamps/noise must be frozen in advance.

comparison.accounting_rule: For a declared scope, count shared reading once, evidenced read adapter deltas once, shared writing-only work once, evidenced write adapter deltas once, build/package/target deltas once, and independent writing validation increment once. The decomposition is bookkeeping, not an additive numerical estimate: no durations, incompatibility-stratum counts or shared-work proportions are measured. Runtime hours, resource availability and owner review are separate. Full-goal R+W must also include historically omitted families; do not reuse the old corpus boundary.

totals.reason: No demonstrated semantic writer or measured encode/preservation/build work, unknown codec/schema/module/target strata, missing matching sources/builders and independent native validation. Historical read ranges are conditional, overlapping and scope-incomplete; no meaningful full-goal ratio or finite bounded total can be justified.

losses: Strict 2024-save-format support excludes older originals and later formats, including the POC's recorded 2021 original; it cannot silently satisfy original-version-preserving writing by converting them.

Historical S12 reports 413/415 versioned RSRC files outside 2024 and XML declarations mostly 2020/2021. These illustrate compatibility loss only, not an estimate of user prevalence or the scope boundary.

Keeping an older immutable original plus a 2024 working copy prevents destruction but does not make the modified 2024 copy usable by the original consumer/runtime. Emitting the edit back to the original format requires additional proven encoding/round-trip compatibility.

A 2024-runtime-only policy differs from 2024-format-only writing: loading older inputs may convert in memory, while later inputs may be incompatible; source formats and output/build versions must be checked independently. Native 2024 access remains unverified.

All artifact families, package/build inputs, source preservation, modules/targets, dependencies and independent checks remain required under the version fallback. Newer-only source features, absent originals/build tools or unavailable target runtimes are not solved by choosing 2024.

Headless 2026 compilation evidence neither provisions 2024 nor permits source authoring under the recorded container restrictions. Offline editing feasibility is separate from lawful/provisioned native build and execution capability.
unresolved_costs: preserving/re-emitting older source versions if required
matching build inputs and module/target tools
fallback.decision_limit: Only conditional reduction in evidenced version-specific work is supportable. No substantial-time difference is established, no numeric threshold exists, and owner silence or ordinary change acceptance is not fallback/method acceptance.

procedure: Recheck original and parser/input pins; stop on mismatch without substituting another VI.

Use the pinned Resources loader on that one original. Record resource IDs, byte lengths and raw version-field bytes for every vers and LVSR entry; decode each with the matching pinned class, retaining both values rather than selecting the convenient one.

Publish one original-hash-to-version-evidence record, including agreement/disagreement, missing or duplicate fields and the exact parser revision/command. Mark authoritative native save-version confirmation unavailable unless independent evidence actually establishes it; do not turn field agreement into native compatibility.
next_measurement.observable_result: A single WM1 evidence record containing actual raw declarations and decoded version tuple(s), or a precise parse/absence/conflict result. It narrows the existing unknown-version input and tells the next shaper whether independent authoritative version evidence is still needed. It does not demonstrate creation/modification, confirmed consumer bindings or 2024 compatibility.
next_measurement.stop_condition: Stop after that one original record, or immediately on a pin mismatch/parse failure. Do not branch into other fixtures, native execution, corpus research or product serialization. Save unavailable authority explicitly instead of choosing vers or LVSR by assumption.
next_measurement.decisive_uncertainty_and_unavailable_exp: The dominant time uncertainty is whether semantic encoding plus integrity/cache preservation can be implemented and reused across save formats. The smallest discriminating native input would be an independently authored, documented same-save-version one-change pair with fixed terminals/types, normal/separate-code settings and full resource diffs; a later changed artifact must undergo separately provisioned original-version load and behavior checks. Comparing such a pair can expose candidate dependencies but cannot alone prove general rules. No such controlled pair/native capability is staged, so this is not the ready follow-up, no new owner request is made, and the WM1 metadata audit must not be sold as a decisive writer measurement.
next_measurement.resume: Read these outputs and the saved POC limits. Perform only the one WM1 version audit if input pins still match; do not rerun closed reviews or POC corpus searches. Independently review this estimate before using it in any fallback proposal. Restore live-goal context through normal staging when available, without claiming parity now.
